system.of: Taking part in patterns you cannot see whole.
system.note: The system is a lens, never true or false in itself. Physics, biology, a marriage are interpretations of it; each interpretation is a claim that can be tested. Its theorems are moves, not facts.

axioms.name: Repetition builds
axioms.statement: Small local acts, repeated with no plan of the whole, make large forms. A form lasts only while the repetition does.

statedIn.anchor: Small things, repeated without a master plan, build large things.

sources.says: A one percent daily change compounds to a very large difference over a year, in either direction.
A few simple organizing principles can produce wildly diverse self-organizing structures.
Conway's Game of Life: simple local rules per cell produce the whole pattern.
The chaos game: stepping halfway toward a random pole, repeated, draws a fractal.
A response changes the next situation, so a slight improvement feeds itself over time.

tensions.says: Reported by a shelf note, not verified at passage level: individual-level fixes draw attention away from changing the rules.

axioms.name: Relation is real
axioms.statement: What repeats together makes something neither part holds alone, and nothing affects without being affected.

statedIn.anchor: What repeats together becomes something new
you cannot affect without being affected

sources.says: A whole arises from relationships between lower-level things as a new independent thing; cites D. H. Lawrence on love as a third thing two people create.
A marriage has no mass or shape and is still as real as a desk or a drop of water.
A system is elements, interconnections and a purpose; it is more than the sum of its parts.
Interbeing: nothing exists separately; caring for another is caring for yourself.
The sense of a separate self depends on not noticing how much of it overlaps with other selves.

axioms.name: Form becomes rule
axioms.statement: A finished form is the material of the next scale, and a threshold changes what the same rule builds.

statedIn.anchor: A Global Form at one scale is a Local Rule at the next

sources.says: At each level a system shows organized state and behavior, which is the same as being a part in a larger system one level up.
Self-organizing systems generate hierarchy: subsystems aggregated into larger subsystems, cell to organ to person to group.
Hierarchies evolve from the lowest level up.
Small changes often appear to make no difference until a critical threshold is crossed.
In complex systems effects build nonlinearly; small events can produce disproportionately large changes.
Tipping is a special case of critical-mass phenomena, with different cross-over points per person.

axioms.name: Chance remains
axioms.statement: Repetition shifts the odds across many attempts and never removes the roll. A little chance inside a rule is what lets its form survive.
axioms.note: Admitted by Sean, 2026-10-09. The manuscript already treats it as a foundation: it is the Fourth Iteration.

sources.says: An exceptional season was probably helped by luck, and luck does not repeat on demand.
People are pattern seekers who reject the idea that a regular-looking sequence came from a random process.
Managing yourself well holds no guarantee of prosperity; things regress toward the mean.
Luck matters. Habits are only the largest factor within your control.
Even pure skill has a probability of success; every action carries some risk.
Ecosystems are resilient partly through rich genetic variability, which lets them learn and evolve.

axioms.name: Worth is the measure
axioms.statement: A repetition is judged by whether it is worth repeating for its own sake, now.

statedIn.anchor: Would I be willing to repeat exactly this, unchanged, indefinitely?

sources.says: A values-focused life is more fulfilling than a goal-focused one because the journey itself is appreciated.
Practice so that every breath, step and action is fulfilling in itself.
There is only minimal control over the rewards for work, so the work has to be its own reason.

tensions.says: Reward is on the other side of sacrifice; response comes before reward. Pulls toward deferral.

axioms.note: The Seventh Iteration already says the universe supplies no meaning and the noticing self makes it.

theorems.name: Leverage
theorems.statement: Some places in a nested pattern move everything built on them; most move almost nothing.
theorems.derivation: Forms are built by repetition, what they build is real, and each becomes material for the next scale. A change near the root therefore reaches every leaf, and a change at a leaf reaches nothing above it.

statedIn.anchor: what the first three pillars make unavoidable

theorems.name: Perspective
theorems.statement: Every view is from one position inside the pattern. Depth comes only from holding more than one.
theorems.derivation: You are a part of a larger form. A part acts only on what is near it. The form has properties no part contains. So no part holds the whole it belongs to, and that includes its view of another person, who is a whole too. What two views make together is itself a Third Thing: depth that neither view has.
theorems.note: Named by Sean, 2026-10-09, who placed it as derived from the pillars, not beside them. It was briefly held as an axiom called "Frames are private". The derivation assumes a noticing mind is a part like any other, which The Woven Self asserts.

statedIn.anchor: You are a loop. You build a tree.
You are a loop. You build a tree.

sources.says: Minds deal with simplified models of reality, not reality, and mostly do not notice.
No one can read your mind, and the same limit may apply to reading your own.
Our models match the world well enough to succeed and still fall far short of representing it.
The observing self registers experience directly; the thinking self produces thoughts about it.
What is available about another person is their behavior, which can be observed more consciously.

mantras.name: Watch it run
mantras.instruction: See the pattern while it is running, before touching it.

mantras.name: Tend the act
mantras.instruction: Change the small repeated thing, not the outcome.
mantras.blindSpot: Blaming a person for what their conditions produce.

mantras.name: Tend the between
mantras.instruction: Fix how two sides translate each other, not the people.
mantras.blindSpot: Repairing a relationship that should be left.

mantras.name: Walk the loop
mantras.instruction: Trace it round to where it started.
mantras.blindSpot: Treating everything as a loop, or taking the blame for harm done to you.

mantras.name: Mind what adds up
mantras.instruction: Settle what can cancel; be deliberate about what only accumulates.

mantras.name: Check the size
mantras.instruction: A change of scale changes what the same act builds.
mantras.blindSpot: Waiting on a threshold with no limit set in advance.

mantras.name: Check the stand-in
mantras.instruction: Ask whether the picture, the measure or the means still matches what it stands for.

mantras.name: Make it worth repeating
mantras.instruction: Ask whether you would repeat exactly this, unchanged, indefinitely, and whether it is yours or owed.

mantras.name: Find the other pole
mantras.instruction: Every pattern, these included, can build or corrode. Look for the side you are not seeing.
mantras.blindSpot: Looking for a second pole on something that has stopped running.
